question: What's the right SDR-to-AE ratio at a $5M ARR seed-stage company?
answer:
**1 SDR per 2.5–3.5 AEs (1:3 ratio) at $5M ARR.** That's 4–5 SDRs supporting 12–15 AEs. Seed-stage companies can't afford 1:1 (too expensive); they use SDRs primarily for lead qualification, not volume generation. As you scale to $20M–$50M ARR, SDR-to-AE ratio converges to 1:2 (one SDR supporting two AEs, or every AE spending 30% self-prospecting). **The Math Behind 1:3 at $5M ARR:** **Baseline:** - 12–15 AEs (needed to maintain $5M ARR + growth) - $300k–$400k per-AE quota - $3.6M–$6M pipeline coverage target (3x quota) = need $45M–$60M total pipeline **Pipeline Creation (Where SDRs Fit):** - Each SDR generates 15–20 SALs (Sales-Accepted Leads) per month - Each SAL has 40%–50% conversion to booked demo (6–10 demos per SAL) - Each booked demo has 60%–70% hold rate (AE attends) = 8–12 AQL (Accepted Qualified Leads) per SDR/month - Each AQL has 25%–35% conversion to sales opportunity = 2–4 opps per SDR/month - Average opp size $50k–$100k ARR (at $5M ARR stage) = $100k–$400k pipeline per SDR per month **Annualized SDR Pipeline:** - 1 SDR × $100k–$400k pipeline/month × 12 months = $1.2M–$4.8M annual pipeline per SDR - Conservative: 1 SDR generates $1.8M pipeline/year (mid-range) - 5 SDRs × $1.8M = $9M pipeline annually - Team of 15 AEs closing 25%–30% of pipeline = $2.25M–$2.7M ARR from SDR-sourced deals - That covers ~45–55% of $5M growth (rest is expansion/self-sourcing/partner) **Why 1:3 (Not 1:1 or 1:5)?** **1:1 SDR-to-AE Ratio (Overstaffed at $5M ARR)** - 12–15 AEs needs 12–15 SDRs - Cost: 12–15 SDRs × $50k OTE = $600k–$750k annual SDR comp - Only feasible if you have $30M–$50M ARR (can support dedicated SDR teams) - At $5M ARR, this is 12–15% of total revenue. Too expensive. **1:5 SDR-to-AE Ratio (Understaffed at $5M ARR)** - 12–15 AEs with only 2–3 SDRs - 2–3 SDRs generate $3.6M–$5.4M pipeline/year - Not enough to support 12–15 AEs; they must self-source 50%+ of pipeline - AEs become part-time hunters, part-time closers (loses focus) - Quota attainment drops; churn increases **1:3 SDR-to-AE Ratio (Optimal at $5M ARR)** - 12–15 AEs with 4–5 SDRs - 4–5 SDRs generate $7.2M–$9M pipeline/year - Covers 40–50% of AE pipeline needs - AEs spend 20–30% time self-prospecting (rest closing) - Cost: 4–5 SDRs × $50k OTE = $200k–$250k (4–5% of revenue; reasonable) **Staffing Matrix (By ARR Stage):** | Company Stage | ARR | AEs | SDRs | Ratio | SDR Cost % | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Seed-stage | $1M–$5M | 3–15 | 1–2 | 1:5–1:3 | 2–4% | | Series A | $5M–$15M | 12–30 | 4–8 | 1:3–1:2 | 3–5% | | Series B | $15M–$40M | 30–60 | 8–20 | 1:2–1:1.5 | 4–6% | | Series C | $40M–$100M | 60–100 | 20–50 | 1:2–1:1 | 5–8% | **Important: At $5M ARR, SDRs are Often Overqualified** At seed stage, many companies hire SDRs from strong backgrounds (previous SalesForce SDRs, HubSpot reps). You can't use them on full outbound volume generation (that's inefficient). Instead: 1. **Lead qualification:** Inbound leads from events/content → SDR qualifies 3–5 calls → hands to AE 2. **Account research:** SDR builds ICP, identifies accounts, does account-based outbound → AE takes meeting 3. **Demo scheduling:** SDR books 5–10 demos/week for AE demo slots 4. **Secondary outreach:** SDR re-engages cold prospects after 30 days (AE didn't move forward) **Avoid:** Using qualified SDRs purely on volume outbound ("Call 100 people/day"). You'll burn them out; they'll leave for AE roles or better SDR shops. **Territory Model (How SDRs Support AEs at $5M ARR):** **Option A: Vertical SDRs (1–2 SDRs per vertical)** - Vertical 1 (Healthcare): 1 SDR + 3–4 AEs - Vertical 2 (FinServ): 1 SDR + 3–4 AEs - Vertical 3 (Retail): 1 SDR + 3–4 AEs - Vertical 4 (Other): 0–1 SDR + 2–3 AEs (SDRs handle expansion/SMB self-source) **Benefit:** SDR learns healthcare ICP deeply; AEs in that vertical get warmer leads **Risk:** Vertical strategy limits (what if healthcare is only 20% of market?) **Option B: Inbound + Expansion SDRs (1–2 SDRs dedicated to non-new-business)** - 3–4 SDRs handle all inbound leads (events, demo requests, content, paid ads) - 0–1 SDR handles expansion/upsell (works with CS team to identify expansion opps for AEs) - AEs do 50% cold prospecting, 50% closing (self-source territory) **Benefit:** Predictable inbound pipeline; AEs always have warm leads **Risk:** Depends on inbound volume (may be too small at $5M ARR stage) **Option C: Hybrid (Most Common at Seed)** - 2 SDRs do inbound qualification + light outbound - 2–3 AEs do heavy outbound (prospecting) + closing - SDRs focus on qualification (phone + initial demo prep), not prospecting volume **SDR Comp at Seed Stage:** | Component | Amount | Notes | |---|---|---| | Base Salary | $32k–$38k | Lower than mid-market SDRs; seed-stage budgets | | Demos Booked | $300–$500 per demo held | 15–20 demos/month = $5k–$10k/month | | SALs Accepted | $500–$750 per SAL | 15–20 SALs/month = $7.5k–$15k/month | | Quarterly Bonus | $2k–$3k if targets hit | Pipeline quality gate | | **Total OTE** | **$50k–$60k** | vs. $80k+ at Series B | **Hiring SDRs at Seed (Challenges):** 1. **Ambition mismatch:** Strong SDRs want to become AEs in 18 months. At $5M ARR, AE slots are limited (maybe 1–2 promotions/year). Seed-stage companies must hire SDRs who want to stay SDRs, or plan fast promotion. 2. **Training burden:** At seed, you have 1 VP Sales and 1 Sales Manager. Training 4–5 SDRs falls on the VP Sales + 1–2 senior AEs. Burn-out risk. 3. **Attrition:** Expect 30–50% SDR turnover at seed stage (bad comp, lack of career growth, training time). Budget for constant recruiting. **When to Scale SDR Headcount (Seed to Series A):** Increase SDRs from 2–3 to 4–6 when: 1. **AE pipeline stalls:** AEs closing <$300k/quarter (from self-source + SDR leads) 2. **SDR demand is visible:** 3 SDRs are at 120%+ targets; add 1–2 more to hit 1:3 ratio 3. **Inbound volume climbs:** If inbound leads double, hire dedicated inbound SDRs **Red Flag: Over-scaling SDRs at Seed** Don't hire 6–8 SDRs at $5M ARR "to scale to $10M." You'll burn cash, churn SDRs (not enough AE slots to promote), and waste 6 months training. Grow SDR headcount gradually (1 every 3–6 months) as pipeline demand increases. ```mermaid flowchart TB A["$5M ARR Company
